The final stable-boundary audit independently reproduced a known generated-constructor opening on ClaimLedger at 2c4b74f9; relevant source bytes are unchanged at eb48a562/bfbcb121. The historical population/probe bead bd-01M183VBPNEAPT5JNQMBMYMKQ9 is closed and did not repair this type. The primary agent independently recompiled and reproduced the consequence.

External Mirror/fromProduct can create hidden map entries, duplicate order entries or keys different from ClaimMeta.id. Hidden entry: size=0 and all empty, but lookup succeeds; JsonLines.claims emits zero bytes and readClaims loses it. Duplicate order writes duplicate claims and reload refuses; miskeyed roundtrip changes the lookup key. Direct new/apply/copy refuse. Normal empty.add/addAll, duplicate refusal and codec roundtrip controls pass. No current study-data occurrence is established; model and reader producers use empty.addAll.

Acceptance: make ledger key/order/identity integrity hold for every publicly constructible ClaimLedger; prefer final non-case class with private constructor and existing empty/add/addAll operations. Keep public reads/equality deliberately. External positive-controlled new/apply/copy/fromProduct/Mirror refusal tests; retain hidden/duplicate/miskeyed and roundtrip witnesses as appropriate; compiled guard mutation or discriminating old-code reproduction, scoped portable tests and consumer review. BLOCK for stable checked-ledger integrity; FOLLOW-UP for currently qualified study path. Evidence: docs/refactor/evidence/stability-audit-20261014/claim-ledger-probe/{assessment.json,run.log,parent-run.log} and constructor-judgment.md A1.
set.title: Close ClaimLedger product-construction bypass before stable API freeze
